And after all the weather was ideal, for they could not have had a more perfect day for a garden party if they had ordered it. <break time="0.8s" /> The air was windless and warm, the sky was without a cloud, and the gardener had been up since dawn, mowing the lawns and sweeping them until they seemed to shine. <break time="0.8s" /> Before breakfast was even over, the men came to put up the marquee, and Missus Sheridan, who wanted the children to arrange everything themselves, told them to treat her as an honored guest. <break time="0.8s" /> Laura, who was considered the artistic one in the family, ran out to meet the four workmen, still holding a piece of bread and butter in her hand. <break time="0.8s" /> She tried to sound businesslike by copying her mothers voice, but it sounded so affected that she felt ashamed and stammered like a little girl instead. <break time="0.8s" /> When she suggested the lily lawn, the tall, lanky, freckled workman looked around and said that a marquee there would not be conspicuous enough. <break time="0.8s" /> In the end he chose a place against the karaka trees, and Laura was sorry, because the trees, with their broad gleaming leaves and clusters of yellow fruit, would be hidden. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the tall workman pinched a sprig of lavender and smelled it, and Laura, deeply charmed, wondered how many of the men she knew would ever have done such a thing. <break time="0.8s" /> It was all the fault of these absurd class distinctions, she decided, and to show how much at home she felt, she took a big bite of her bread and butter.

When Laura was called to the telephone, she met her brother Laurie in the hall, and, giving him a small quick squeeze, she cried, Oh, I do love parties. <break time="0.8s" /> On the telephone she invited Kitty Maitland to lunch, while her mothers voice floated down the stairs, telling Laura that Kitty must wear the sweet hat she had worn last Sunday. <break time="0.8s" /> The house was alive with quick steps and running voices, and little spots of sunlight played on the inkpot and the silver photograph frame, as if they too were enjoying the day. <break time="0.8s" /> A man from the florist arrived with a wide tray full of pink canna lilies, so many that Laura cried out in surprise, and her mother confessed that she had ordered them herself. <break time="0.8s" /> I saw them in a shop window yesterday, said Missus Sheridan, and I suddenly thought that for once in my life I would have enough canna lilies. <break time="0.8s" /> In the drawing room Jose tested the piano by singing a sad song about a weary life, and then she smiled a brilliant, unsympathetic smile, sure that she was in good voice. <break time="0.8s" /> In the kitchen there were fifteen different kinds of sandwiches, and the cook, who had made every one of them, smiled with pride when Jose praised her work. <break time="0.8s" /> When the man from Godbers brought cream puffs, the cook let each girl have one, and soon they were licking whipped cream from their fingers.
